summary: A proposed first part of a Network Standard Graphics Protocol from the Network Graphics Group. It describes the stream of 8-bit bytes sent from an application on a serving host to a display package on a using host, covering only the simplest forms of graphics data. It was replaced by RFC 493.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 292 proposes commands for sending simple graphics from one host to another as a stream of bytes. It covers output only and was intended to support experimentation.

questions: what commands did graphics protocol level 0 define
subtitle: A proposed byte-stream protocol for sending simple graphics to another host.

tldr.problem: The Network Graphics Group needed a common format for sending graphics output from an application host to a display host.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 292 proposes a sequence of 8-bit bytes containing commands such as erase, move, draw, dot, and text, using logical coordinates.
tldr.outcome: The document describes only the simplest output functions and calls itself a basis for experimentation, not a finished protocol. It was later obsoleted by RFC 493.

today: RFC 292 is historic and was obsoleted by RFC 493. It documents an early proposal for a network graphics output byte stream.

sections.title: Sending Graphics Output
sections.content: RFC 292 describes part of a proposed Network Standard Graphics Protocol. An application on a Serving Host sends a sequence of 8-bit bytes to a display package on a Using Host. The RFC covers simple output forms, not graphics input or how to establish the connection.
sections.plainLanguage: One computer sends drawing commands to another computer's display. This first proposal covers simple graphics output only.

sections.title: Commands and Coordinates
sections.content: A command consists of a command byte followed by its arguments. The logical coordinate system uses two dimensions, with the origin at the center of the display and coordinates from minus one-half to just less than plus one-half. The receiving host maps logical coordinates to its physical device.
sections.plainLanguage: Each instruction starts with a command byte, followed by the needed values. The receiving computer converts the shared logical coordinates to its own screen.

sections.title: Level 0 Drawing Commands
sections.content: Level 0 includes commands to erase the screen, move without drawing, draw a line, display a dot, display text, and end a picture. Move, draw, and dot commands can use absolute positions or relative changes. The proposal aims to keep Level 0 simple to implement.
sections.plainLanguage: The basic commands clear the display, move a beam, draw lines or dots, show text, and mark the end of a picture.

sections.title: An Experimental Proposal
sections.content: The document says the protocol was not intended as a finished specification. It proposes levels so a host implementing a higher level would also implement lower levels, and states that the protocol may need to change because it is experimental.
sections.plainLanguage: This was a starting point for experiments, not a final graphics standard. The proposal expected the protocol to grow in levels and possibly change.
